steps.title: Как устроено реальное условие
steps.html:
Часть с ifРезультатПример
if + present simplewill / won'tIf you cycle every day, you will live longer.
if + present simplemay / might / couldIf you cycle every day, you may add two years.
if + present simplecanIf a country has high taxes, it can provide free healthcare.
if + present simpleповелительноеIf you have an important decision, make it early in the day.
unless / as long as / provided thatте же формы результатаUnless everyone has enough, money doesn't help.

steps.title: Как это работает
steps.html:
Обе части о будущем, но показывает это только результат. В части с if — Present Simple; именно здесь и ошибаются.

unless = if not. Не удваивайте отрицание: unless you don't hurry — ошибка.

as long as и provided that добавляют оттенок соблюдённого условия — договорённости, правила.

Любая часть может идти первой. Если первой стоит часть с if — после неё запятая; если второй — запятой нет.

items.text: If people spend more than an hour travelling to work, they are generally less content.
Unless you have some close friendships, you will find it hard to be happy.
If you do regular exercise outdoors, you'll be able to work more efficiently.
People tend to be happier if they are in a long-term relationship.
If people are active in work and free time, they'll probably be healthier.

steps.title: The happiest country in the world
steps.html:
Прочитайте один раз. Последний абзац поворачивает аргумент — обратите на него внимание.

Denmark comes first in the World Happiness Report most years, and the reason is not the weather. If you rank countries by sunshine, Denmark finishes near the bottom of Europe. So what are the other countries in the list actually measuring?

Money comes into it, but not in the way people expect. A country with very little poverty tends to score well, and a strong economy certainly helps. Look further down the list, though, and Mexico sits above the United States. Money does not make a population happy unless everyone has enough of it: large differences between rich and poor make people less content, whatever the average income says.

A rich country is also not automatically a country that looks after its people. Denmark pays high taxes and gets free healthcare, cheap childcare and paid leave for both parents after a birth. You may not believe you will be happier if you pay more tax. As a country, you will.

Then there is time. The Danes work a thirty-seven hour week on average, which leaves real leisure time, and they spend a lot of it with other people. Half of all journeys to work and school in Copenhagen are made by bicycle — if you cycle for thirty minutes a day, doctors estimate you may add one to two years to your life. In winter the word people use is hygge: candles, warmth, food and company, in a country where it is dark by four.

None of this is a secret, and none of it is free. Provided that a society is willing to pay for the childcare and accept the taxes, most of the list can be copied. The part that cannot be copied is the last one: more than forty per cent of Danes use their leisure time to do voluntary work for their neighbours. Unless people want to, no government can arrange it.

In winter the word people use is hygge: candles, warmth, food and company, in a country where it is dark by four.

None of this is a secret, and none of it is free. Provided that a society is willing to pay for the childcare and accept the taxes, most of the list can be copied. The part that cannot be copied is the last one: more than forty per cent of Danes use their leisure time to do voluntary work for their neighbours. Unless people want to, no government can arrange it.

The happiest country in the world

Denmark comes first in the World Happiness Report most years, and the reason is not the weather. If you rank countries by sunshine, Denmark finishes near the bottom of Europe. So what are the other countries in the list actually measuring?

Money comes into it, but not in the way people expect. A country with very little poverty tends to score well, and a strong economy certainly helps. Look further down the list, though, and Mexico sits above the United States. Money does not make a population happy unless everyone has enough of it: large differences between rich and poor make people less content, whatever the average income says.

steps.title: Ответьте вслух.
items: Что из статьи сильнее всего изменило бы вашу страну? Используйте if.
Согласились бы вы на более высокие налоги ради бесплатных детсадов и медицины? При каком условии?
Закончите: I'll be happier this year as long as…

steps.title: Теперь ответьте одним высказыванием. Запишите себя.
steps.sub: Используйте if, unless и as long as хотя бы по разу.
items: If my country … , people will probably … .
I'd support higher taxes as long as … .

steps.title: Урок 22 пройден
items: Я говорю о результате реального условия.
Я верно использую unless, as long as и provided that.
Я могу говорить о факторах счастья.
Я при этом верно строю вопросы.
